\section[scientia, scientiae]{scientia, scientiae — knowledge, skill}

\label{lesson:LA-C407-scientia}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for painstaking, then the Latin for careless.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: scientia, scientiae}
\textbf{scientia, scientiae} — \textquotedblleft{}knowledge, skill\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Scientia rērum ūtilis est.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Knowledge of things is useful.}
\end{quote}

\emph{scientia, scientiae} f., built on \emph{sciēns}, knowing. English \emph{science}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{scientia} is built on \emph{sciēns} \textquotedblleft{}knowing\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), the participle of \emph{sciō} \textquotedblleft{}to know\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short). English \emph{science} comes from it through French.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{scientia, scientiae}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{scientia, scientiae}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{scientia, scientiae}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Latin for painstaking, then the Latin for careless, then say \emph{scientia, scientiae} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does scientia, scientiae mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Knowledge, skill\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[intellegentia, intellegentiae]{intellegentia, intellegentiae — understanding, intelligence}

\label{lesson:LA-C407-intellegentia}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for careless, then the Latin for knowledge.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: intellegentia, intellegentiae}
\textbf{intellegentia, intellegentiae} — \textquotedblleft{}understanding, intelligence\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Intellegentia eius omnēs superat.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{His understanding is greater than anyone's.}
\end{quote}

\emph{intellegentia, intellegentiae} f., the noun of \emph{intellegō}. English \emph{intelligence}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{intellegentia} is the noun built on \emph{intellegō} \textquotedblleft{}to understand\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB; Lewis \& Short), from \emph{inter} \textquotedblleft{}between\textquotedblright{} and \emph{legō} \textquotedblleft{}to pick\textquotedblright{}: to choose between. English \emph{intelligence} comes from it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Latin for careless, then the Latin for knowledge, then say \emph{intellegentia, intellegentiae} again

\section[doctrīna, doctrīnae]{doctrīna, doctrīnae — teaching, learning; a doctrine}

\label{lesson:LA-C407-doctrina}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for knowledge, then the Latin for understanding.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: doctrīna, doctrīnae}
\textbf{doctrīna, doctrīnae} — \textquotedblleft{}teaching, learning; a doctrine\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Vir magnae doctrīnae erat.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{He was a man of great learning.}
\end{quote}

\emph{doctrīna, doctrīnae} f., built on \emph{doctor}, a teacher, from \emph{doceō}. English \emph{doctrine}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{doctrīna} is built on \emph{doctor} \textquotedblleft{}a teacher\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), which comes from \emph{doceō} \textquotedblleft{}to teach\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short). English \emph{doctrine} comes from it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[īnscītia, īnscītiae]{īnscītia, īnscītiae — ignorance, lack of skill}

\label{lesson:LA-C407-inscitia}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for understanding, then the Latin for teaching.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: īnscītia, īnscītiae}
\textbf{īnscītia, īnscītiae} — \textquotedblleft{}ignorance, lack of skill\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Īnscītiā nautae nāvis periit.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The ship was lost through the sailor's lack of skill.}
\end{quote}

\emph{īnscītia, īnscītiae} f., built on \emph{īnscītus}, not knowing, from \emph{in-} and \emph{sciō}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{īnscītia} is built on \emph{īnscītus} \textquotedblleft{}unknowing\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB; Lewis \& Short), from \emph{in-} \textquotedblleft{}not\textquotedblright{} and the root of \emph{sciō} \textquotedblleft{}to know\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[imitor, imitārī]{imitor, imitārī — to imitate, to copy}

\label{lesson:LA-C407-imitor}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for teaching, then the Latin for ignorance.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: imitor, imitārī}
\textbf{imitor, imitārī} — \textquotedblleft{}to imitate, to copy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Fīlius patrem imitātur.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The son imitates his father.}
\end{quote}

Deponent: \emph{imitor, imitārī, imitātus sum}, with the accusative. English \emph{imitate}.

\begin{cousinweb}
The origin of \emph{imitor} is not settled; Lewis \& Short give no sure account, though it is often grouped with the word for an image. English \emph{imitate} comes from it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{imitor, imitārī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{imitor, imitārī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{imitor, imitārī}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Latin for teaching, then the Latin for ignorance, then say \emph{imitor, imitārī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
